messages:
maria: Heads up — seeing a boot regression on ~6 nodes in the us-east2 GPU pool after the 550 driver + CUDA 11.8 rollout. Nodes stuck in initramfs, DKMS rebuild errors in the boot logs :grimacing:

tyler: Can you paste the journal snippet so we can see the failure mode?

maria: sure, grabbed the tail of journalctl from node-117:
```
Mar 17 21:49:01 node-117 dkms: nvidia: running module build for kernel 5.15.0-1024-gke
Mar 17 21:49:02 node-117 dkms: Error! Could not find the necessary dkms.conf file.
Mar 17 21:49:02 node-117 dkms: kernel header path missing: /lib/modules/5.15.0-1024-gke/build
Mar 17 21:49:05 node-117 kernel: nvidia: module verification failed: signature and required key missing
Mar 17 21:49:06 node-117 initramfs: Failed to load module nvidia, aborting
Mar 17 21:49:06 node-117 initramfs: panic: kernel modules failed to load
Mar 17 21:49:06 node-117 containerd: ERROR: NCCL WARN Call to epoll_wait failed
```

infra-bot: Deploy audit: driver-rollout/2026-03-17-22:10 started; 72% of hosts processed so far.

sam: running `dkms status` on one affected host shows `nvidia, 550.30: added` but `dkms build` fails against some kernel variants; looks like mixed kernel headers across the fleet.

olivia: Staging canary passed but prod has mixed kernel image versions (some nodes still on older gke kernel). My hunch: kernel header mismatch + module signing problem.

karthik: Quick workaround that worked on node-121: installed matching linux-headers, ran `update-initramfs -u -k $(uname -r)`, signed the module with our key (`kmodsign`) and rebooted — node came back clean.

maria: We need decision: rollback or patch? We already have ~120 GPU pod evictions queued and inference throughput dropped ~30%.

tyler: Immediate ops plan: taint affected nodes so sched won't place new pods: `kubectl taint nodes -l pool=gpu critical=regression:NoSchedule` then spike fallback capacity in us-west1 (p4 fallback) to preserve SLOs. I'll coordinate with capacity.

devx: note — model-serving pods reported NCCL timeouts, logs show `NCCL WARN Allreduce timeout` and `failed to open device /dev/infiniband/rdma_cm` on some hosts. This smells like driver/kernel RDMA incompat.

sam: saw `nvidia-peermem: probe failed -22` on three nodes too.

oncall-bot: Incident created INC-2026-0317-55. Paging infra-leads and gpu-oncall.

olivia: Proposed: pause the 550 rollout immediately, and schedule a controlled rollback to 535 for affected hosts. Requesting emergency quota to spin up 10 p4 instances in us-west1 for traffic migration.

karthik: I'll prepare a rollback script: `apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535 && update-initramfs -u -k all && kmodsign --sign-key /etc/keys/infra-keystore.pem /lib/modules/*/kernel/drivers/video/nvidia.ko && reboot`. Will add a precheck: `test -f /lib/modules/$(uname -r)/build/include/linux/version.h` before proceeding.

maria: progress update — rolled back node-117 to 535 and rebooted; it came back and most pods recovered. LGTM so far.

tyler: follow-up: add kernel-header sanity check to the rollout job, and add a DKMS build step in the CI gating the driver image. Also add a canary that specifically tests RDMA/NCCL repros.

maria: thanks all — keep posting status here. tagging @infra-team for visibility :thumbsup:
